title: Enabling On-Tiny-Device Model Personalization via Gradient Condensing and Alternant Partial Update
problem: On-device training and model personalization on tiny embedded devices (e.g., <1 MB SRAM, 2 MB Flash); multi-layer backpropagation incurs prohibitive computational and memory cost on resource-constrained devices.
motivation: On-device training enables user personalization without server transmission, but backpropagation through multiple layers is prohibitively expensive on tiny embedded systems with severe memory and compute constraints.
method: Algorithm-system co-optimization framework TinyMP: (1) Gradient Condensing reduces gradient map structure complexity and memory consumption while preserving model performance; (2) Alternant Partial Update locally and alternatively selects essential parameters to update without retraining or offline evolutionary search, reducing computation overhead.
key_novelty: Gradient Condensing and Alternant Partial Update techniques enabling efficient on-device fine-tuning on tiny embedded devices with minimal resources.
contributions: Gradient Condensing algorithm reducing backpropagation computational complexity and memory consumption
Alternant Partial Update mechanism for selective parameter updates without retraining
Up to 2.4x speedup on embedded devices (MobileNetV2, MCUNet on OpenMV-H7)
80.8% memory saving and 30.3% accuracy improvement on downstream tasks
primary_theme: On-tiny-device personalization via gradient condensing and partial updates
